blocks.arabic_text: (وَفِي حَدِيثِ طَوِيلٍ) عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عَبَسَةَ السُّلَمِيِّ ﵁ وَفِيهِ مَكَانَ (ثُمَّ كَانَ مَشْيُهُ إِلَي الْمَسْجِدِ وَصَلَاتُهُ نَافِلَةً): فَإِنْ هُوَ قَامَ فَصَلَّي، فَحَمِدَ اللهَ وَأَثْنَي عَلَيْهِ، وَمَجَّدَهُ بِالَّذِي هُوَ لَهُ أَهْلٌ، وَفَرَّغَ قَلْبَهُ لِلّهِ، إِلَّا انْصَرَفَ مِنْ خَطِيئَتِهِ كَهَيْئَتِهِ يَوْمَ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic:
رواه النسائي باب مسح الاذنين مع الراس ...رقم:١٠٣
رواه مسلم باب اسلام عمرو بن عبسة ﵁ رقم:١٩٣٠
blocks.tamil_translation:
Hazrat Abdullah Sunabihi (RA) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “When a believing servant makes Wudu and rinses his mouth, all the sins of his mouth are washed away. When he cleans his nose (nostrils), all the sins of the nose are washed away. When he washes his face, the sins of the face are washed away and go out from the roots of the eyelashes. When he washes his hands, the sins of the hands are washed away and go out from beneath the nails. When he makes masah of the head, the sins of the head are washed away and go out from the ears. When he washes his feet, the sins of the feet are washed away and go out from beneath the toenails. Then, his going to the masjid and his praying will be extra (a cause of additional virtue) for him.' In another narration, through Hazrat Amr ibn Abasah Sulami (RA), it is said: “If, after making Wudu, he stands to pray, praises and glorifies Allah as befits His rank and declares His exaltedness, empties his heart (of all other thoughts) and prays with his attention directed towards Allah, then when he finishes praying he becomes purified of sins like a child born that day.”
Explanation:- Through Wudu, all sins related to the body are forgiven.
